summary:
Reason for this letter: I came across a dedication for FLOW MY TEARS, THE POLICEMAN SAID which may not have reached you. It is the one I want on the book, so here it is: 

The love in this novel is for Tessa, and the love in me is for her, too, and for our little new baby Christopher. They are my little songs. 

On to other matters, now. Diane I am anxious for you to read Stanislaw Lem’s now famous article, “Science Fiction: A Hopeless Case—with Exceptions.” It’s in the current S.F. Commentary. Originally the article in German circulated throughout Europe and may be one of the most important articles on s-f. There are 10 initial pages showing the hopelessness of s-f, and then (I hope you are sitting down when you read this) 19 more pages of “exceptions,” which consists only of me. ME! Lem’s critical articles are being read, and I think my enormous sales in Europe these days stem from his article published there about two years ago. Boy, that paragraph sounds like an ego trip. But he calls me the “one true artist among mere artisans.” I am sure blurb copy could be gleaned from this article. 
Speaking of blurbs, I hate to be the heavy in life—my image as Mr. Nice Guy makes me more comfortable, but honestly, Diane, those flap blurbs or blurb flaps on FLOW MY TEARS—please don’t stop loving me with all the ten­ derness in your great heart if I say they were so badly written that I almost had a seizure. Then the extract from my own book came on the next page and I didn’t recognize ...
